problems.statement: The supervisor bonus penalty (4% per attributed deviation, max 40%, from Feb 2026) created a perverse incentive that suppresses deviation reporting; the zero-deviation record measures suppressed reporting, not quality.

Line 3's 118% attainment is not a superior practice but is produced by undocumented borrowing of 4-7 technicians from Lines 1 and 4 (timesheets charged to home lines); per-technician-hour productivity is unchanged at about 41, so Line 3 is not a template.

Actual quality has deteriorated: customer complaints rose from 11 to 31 ppm, luer-bond leaks concentrate in Line 3 lots, and final-inspection rejections rose; the reality is the opposite of the reported record.

Probable off-record rework (re-bonding leaking subassemblies in the back cage without NCR or device history record entry) is occurring on Line 3, which would be a regulatory and data-integrity violation; this rests on an anonymous report and indirect corroboration, not yet directly verified.

The Quality Manager's explanation that the first-pass quality training program caused the deviation drop is rejected: the drop occurred in February before the March 9 launch, completion was only 40% by June, and complaints and rejections worsened.

The Line 3 supervisor's explanation (5S, huddles, early problem catching) is rejected as the cause: huddles predate 2025, when Line 3 had 38% of deviations, and productivity per technician-hour is flat once borrowed staff are counted.

The new lower-cost tubing supplier explains the quality decline or the purchasing increase: the purchasing rise began in February, before the April 14 switch, the incoming rejection rate differs only 1.1% vs 1.0%, and Lines 2 and 5 on the same tubing show few complaints.
The root bonding-process defect (cure-time variability at luer bonding, CAPA-2025-117) was never fixed and persists; it is probably what the hidden rework is covering.

A climate of fear and failed governance controls (ethics case closed after only the supervisor's denial, plant manager conflicted, retaliation rumours, undocumented informal directives) prevents problems surfacing and blinds leadership.
Leadership relies on a self-reported metric attached to its own incentive and is unaware of or misreading the situation, so the presenting request would institutionalise the problem.

actions.action: Suspend the supervisor bonus deduction tied to deviation reports and replace it with metrics that reward accurate reporting and downstream outcomes such as complaints and final-QC rejections.
actions.rationale: The incentive is the established cause of suppressed reporting and is cheap and reversible to remove.

actions.action: Reopen hotline case 2026-031 under independent investigation (corporate quality or Regulatory, not the Plant Manager): review device history records against purchasing and scrap, inspect the back cage, and interview with anti-retaliation protection.
actions.rationale: This is the cheapest verification of the off-record rework hypothesis and the allegation was never properly tested.

actions.action: Hold the rollout of Line 3 as the template and do not document its practices for other lines.
actions.rationale: Its performance is attributable to borrowed labour and possibly hidden rework, so replication would spread the problem.

actions.action: Assess regulatory exposure: contain suspect Line 3 lots, review shipped lots, and engage Regulatory Affairs and OEM customers on possible notification obligations if rework is confirmed.
actions.rationale: Leaks at the luer bond joint in infusion sets are a patient-safety risk and complaints are rising.

actions.action: Drive CAPA-2025-117 to closure by fixing cure-time variability at the bonding station.
actions.rationale: The root process defect has been open for a year with no change and is the likely source of the leaks.

actions.action: Restore a no-retaliation channel, review the night-shift moves of NCR writers, and make the lending of technicians between lines visible with correct timesheet charging.
actions.rationale: This repairs information flow and labour accounting but is secondary to removing the incentive and verifying the facts.

actions.action: Discipline or terminate the Line 3 supervisor now based on the hotline report.
actions.rationale: The allegation is unverified and anonymous, and acting prematurely would destroy evidence and deepen fear; the incentive design is a leadership-level cause.

actions.action: Credit the training programme and expand it as the explanation of the quality gain.
actions.rationale: The timeline and the complaint data contradict it.

actions.action: Switch back to the previous tubing supplier as the fix.
actions.rationale: The evidence does not support the supplier as the cause.

actions.action: Publicly celebrate the zero-deviation record to customers or auditors.
actions.rationale: The record is likely a reporting artefact and could expose the company to misrepresentation.

nextEvidence: Independent reconciliation of Line 3 device history records and lot traceability against purchasing and scrap of connectors, tubing and adhesive, plus a physical inspection of the back cage and shift-two activity.
Anonymous or protected interviews with Line 3 second-shift technicians and borrowed technicians, and a review of the night-shift reassignment records for former NCR writers.
Line-attributed component and scrap issuance and bonding-station process data (cure time) by line, together with the CAPA-2025-117 status and complaint lot-level traceability.
output.summary: The zero-deviation record is an artefact of the February supervisor bonus penalty, which suppressed reporting. Complaints (11 to 31 ppm), final-QC rejections, and 30% higher component purchases against 9% higher output show quality worsening. Line 3's 118% is explained by undocumented borrowing of 4-7 technicians from Lines 1 and 4; per-hour productivity is unchanged, so it is no template. Probable off-record rework of leaking luer bonds is unverified but strongly indicated, and the 2025 bonding CAPA is still open. Training and tubing explanations fail on timing. Remove the incentive, independently investigate, contain lots, and do not roll out Line 3.
